metadata.description: An OCI image as a fact about the estate: the digest-identified artifact a Container runs, or a Machine boots when its operating system is delivered as an image. A Knowledge class: discovered by a scanner sweep, never provider-realized. The OCI image spec is adopted by reference; the digest is the identity. A Container or Machine that states this digest runs this image: the join is derived and no edge is stored. A SoftwareBillOfMaterials describes the image and lists its packages.

digest.description: The image manifest digest (sha256:…), the immutable correlation id. One record per digest.

tag.description: A tag observed pointing at this digest; advisory, since tags move and digests do not.

registry.description: The registry host serving the image.

os.description: Target OS from the image config (OCI platform.os).

arch.description: Target architecture from the image config (OCI platform.architecture).

adopts.role: the image identity and structure vocabulary this type's digest/reference fields align to

context.purpose: Records an OCI image as a digest-identified fact — the thing a container runs or a machine boots, and the subject its software bill of materials describes.
context.plain_description: One image, identified by its content digest (one observed `tag` is recorded, singular and advisory — tags move, the digest does not). It is knowledge about the estate, discovered by scanning, never provisioned: which `repository` and `registry` it came from and what platform it targets (`os` and `arch`). A container image and a bootable operating-system image are the same kind of artifact and the same class. What is inside the image is not listed here: a SoftwareBillOfMaterials describes the image and lists its packages, so two scans of one image are two documents about one record. That chain is what turns which containers run something shipping a given library from an investigation into a graph walk.
use_when: You need every running container tied to the exact image digest it runs, deduplicated across the fleet.
You need a host that boots an image tied to that image, so a fix is a new image and not a package update.
You need the subject a bill of materials hangs from: image ← document → packages → vulnerabilities.
not_for: The running workload — Container runs an image; this is the image as a fact.
A package inside the image — SoftwarePackage, listed by the image's SoftwareBillOfMaterials.
works_with: Container and Machine — the things that run this image, joined by the digest each one states.
SoftwareBillOfMaterials — the document that describes the image and lists its packages.
